root_idea.summary: A root principle of extension: something stretches either upward in elevation or outward in motion.
root_idea.development: The physical neck represents extension between head and body; this develops into meanings of length, elevation, forward movement, emergence, connection, and an assembled company.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The canonical Quranic nominal is best presented under the singular dictionary citation form عُنُقٌ, whose Quranic plural and inflected forms occur nine times.

senses.definition: The neck: the bodily part joining the head and the body.
senses.usage_conditions: Used literally of a person's or creature's neck, including in expressions about chains, striking, or a person's liability being attached to the neck.

senses.definition: The head or upper part of a person, by metonymy from the neck.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction فَوْقَ الْأَعْنَاقِ, “above the necks,” the necks are explained as the heads; this is a construction-specific metonymic use, not a general replacement of “neck” by “head.”

senses.definition: A company, or the leading and eminent people of a group.
senses.usage_conditions: In فَظَلَّتْ أَعْنَاقُهُمْ لَهَا خَاضِعِينَ, the plural may be understood as their companies or their chiefs and great ones; a literal interpretation as their necks is also reported.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become long in the neck; according to one reported explanation, to be long and thick-necked.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form I verb describing the neck's physical length or thickness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Length of the neck.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal description of neck length.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To proceed while looking down upon something, or to come into view from above.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form II construction involving movement and an elevated or overlooking position.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a cloud to emerge from the main mass of clouds and appear white in the sunlight.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional description of a cloud's emergence into view.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For the buttocks or anus to protrude.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive bodily-use expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For the spathes of palm trees to become long without splitting open.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A botanical Form II use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a partly colored date to ripen nearly to its base, leaving a ring-like remainder around the stem.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of date ripening.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seize someone or an animal by the neck and squeeze the throat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive Form II action; in a reported prophetic expression it may also be interpreted as distressing or treating the creature roughly.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To disappoint someone or thwart what the person sought.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct reported explanation of the same Form II verb, connected lexically with العَنَاقُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To embrace someone, putting the arms around the neck and drawing or pressing the person to oneself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The reciprocal forms describe mutual embracing; some authorities distinguish affectionate عناق from the war-related use of reciprocal forms, while others allow both in either setting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put a collar or other neck-band upon an animal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Especially used of putting a collar on a dog.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To travel at a quick, stretching pace with wide steps; to hasten.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a horse or similar animal and, by extension, of people hastening toward someone or something.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For countries to be or become distant or remote.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported regional or lexical use of the intransitive Form IV verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For the Pleiades to set; for stars to advance toward their setting place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A marked astronomical or figurative use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For corn or grain to become tall and put forth its ears.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative botanical use based on the appearance of a neck or extended growth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For the wind to raise, carry away, and disperse dust.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use associated with rapid sweeping movement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a jerboa or hare to insert its head and neck into, or hide in, its burrow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with the burrow called عَانِقَاءُ and describing concealment by pushing the head and neck into loose earth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put chains upon one's own neck.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional expression for self-imposed bondage or ascetic restraint.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take up an affair with earnestness and commitment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive idiomatic use with an affair or undertaking as object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For an animal to fall into mire and thrust out its neck.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive description of an animal struggling in mud.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For the wind to raise and disperse dust.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported figurative Form VIII use connected with the wide-striding pace called عَنَق.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A stretching or quick pace with wide steps.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used particularly of horses and camels, and also of their manner of travel generally.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A star situated in the neck of the constellation Serpens; the expression is also used of a star in Hydra's neck.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An astronomical naming use based on the neck of a figured constellation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The slender neck of the womb toward the vaginal opening.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The lower portion of a ruminant's stomach.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical term, also called القِبَّةُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The trunks or elongated lower portions of palm trees.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative plural use based on the shape of a neck.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The internodal portions of the stalks of seed crops that have appeared.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A botanical expression describing elongated portions of grain stalks.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The portions of dust raised by the wind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative plural expression for dust columns or masses borne upward by wind.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A portion or projecting mass issuing from a fire.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative expression recorded in a tradition and based on the image of an extended neck.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A current or projecting stream issuing from a river or rivulet.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative expression for an extended portion of flowing water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The first or early part of a season, a person's age, a period, or a historical era.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in expressions such as the beginning of summer, the beginning of a person's sixtieth year, or the early period of time or Islam.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The upper portion of an elevated, elongated tract of sand or similar terrain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A geographic and topographical use derived from the form of a neck.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be coherent or tightly connected, said of speech or language.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic figurative expression in which the parts of speech are pictured as taking hold of one another's necks.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To incline or advance toward someone as a company.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic expression for a group approaching or looking expectantly toward a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A portion or share of good, property, or work.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression may refer to a person's share or precedence in good works.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A female kid or young goat; by extension, a young lamb or kid.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The age range varies among authorities, from newborn or very young to roughly one year; the plural includes عُنُوقٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A small predatory land animal, described as smaller than a leopard or lynx and resembling a badger in some applications.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A zoological term with differing identifications in the lexical sources.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The middle star of the three stars called Banāt Naʿsh al-Kubrā in the tail of Ursa Major.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An astronomical proper name, distinct from the zoological and abstract uses of the word.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A star identified by some as the star in the leg or foot of Andromeda.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate astronomical application of the expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A calamity, misfortune, hard affair, or difficult event; in an idiom, an exorbitant lie.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in expressions describing someone as having encountered calamity or a hard matter, or as having uttered an extravagant falsehood.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Disappointment or failure to obtain what was sought.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in poetic and proverbial expressions such as returning with disappointment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A stony tract or stony ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A geographic use equated with حَرَّةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The poor-rate assessed as two years' due.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported use in an early statement about withholding alms; another transmission has عِقَالًا, meaning one year's poor-rate.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Embracing, with the arms placed around another's neck.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival or descriptive form for the act or its manner; the corresponding verb is عَانَقَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sort of dates.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized expression, with the reading of the headword noted as uncertain in the lexical discussion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A famous day or conflict in Arab history.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed historical name rather than a productive ordinary noun phrase.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A jerboa's burrow or chamber filled with earth or dust, in which the animal conceals itself up to the neck.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may also be applied to a comparable hare burrow; it belongs to the vocabulary of animal burrows.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Long-necked; according to another explanation, long and thick-necked.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to people and other creatures; the feminine is عَنْقَاءُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having a white marking on the neck.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized application to a dog.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A proper name associated with a famous Arab stallion and, in another report, with a wealthy headman; بنات أَعْنَقَ may refer to the stallion's progeny or to women associated with the name.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An onomastic and genealogical use, with variant identifications reported in the lexical tradition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A legendary or unidentifiable bird known chiefly by its name.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression عَنْقَاءُ مُغْرِبٍ is also explained as a fabulous bird, sometimes identified speculatively with an eagle or the Persian sīmurgh.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A calamity or misfortune that carries a person away.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative idiom derived from the legendary bird expression; it is also used simply for a great calamity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A high, long eminence, such as the summit of a mound or the upper part of a tall mountain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A topographical interpretation of عَنْقَاءُ مُغْرِبٌ that rejects the bird interpretation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A plain or soft tract of land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural is تَعَانِيقُ; vowel variants are reported.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hard, elevated ground surrounded by plain or soft land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A topographical noun describing a raised tract extending lengthwise for about a mile or less.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A lofty place from which to observe.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A place-name or descriptive noun for an elevated lookout.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who hastens in obedience and takes a wide range in his work.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative epithet for a believer in a traditional usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Lying ahead of others, said of elongated sand tracts.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or descriptive plural use applied to portions of sand dunes.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A curved piece of rock.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A concrete topographical noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A country in which settlement does not endure because of dryness and barrenness; another report explains it as a distant or remote country.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The sources preserve both the barren-land and remote-country interpretations.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A collar placed around a dog's neck.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized noun for an animal collar.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A small elongated and elevated tract of sand lying before or in front of the main sands.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A topographical term with variant plural formations reported.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A designation for certain Arab horses.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A singular adjective or nisbah associated with the plural مَعَانِقُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A small creeping creature marked by neck-rings or whiteness around the neck.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lexical discussion identifies it with small creatures that gnaw holes in leather water or milk vessels.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Long or elongated, applied to forward-stretching sand tracts.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The correctly reported application is to حِبَال, elongated tracts of sand, rather than mountains.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hectic fever.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Explicitly identified as a post-classical usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who or that which moves at the good, wide-stepping pace called عَنَق; hence a hastening person or group.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to horses, camels, people, and groups; it may also describe one hastening after a pursued object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A ewe or goat that bears young goats.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized animal epithet, perhaps implying frequent production according to the lexical explanation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place where the upper portions of elongated mountain or sand tracts emerge from a mirage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A topographical noun describing landforms appearing through or beyond the mirage.

cautions: In Quran 26:4, أَعْنَاقُهُمْ has competing interpretations: literal necks, companies, or chiefs and great ones; the company/chiefs sense is explicitly attested but should not erase the literal reading.
The interpretation of فَوْقَ الْأَعْنَاقِ as “above the heads” is specific to that Quranic construction and does not make “head” the ordinary meaning of عُنُقٌ.
